Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Rust web application. Start in the `/app` Git repository: it has a minimal Cargo project (`quizzy`) and no app yet. Rust (stable), Cargo, SQLite (the library and the CLI), and Chromium are installed. You can download crates from crates.io; other network access is blocked. Fetch and build all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the build, the database, and so on) and runs the app in release mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`. It must work offline (for example, `cargo build --release --offline`), and it should start in a few minutes at most.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

# Quizzy Moderator Release - Design Notes

## Architecture
- Rust + Axum 0.8 + Tokio + rusqlite (system SQLite, no bundled build for speed)
- Single binary `quizzy`, single file `src/main.rs` (~1300 lines)
- Per-request SQLite connections to `storage/quizzy.sqlite` with WAL + foreign_keys
- Stateless preview via URL query params (`q`, `score`, `picked`), no session storage
- Basic auth middleware for all `/moderate*` (401 + WWW-Authenticate on fail)
- Static assets embedded via `include_str!/include_bytes!` served at `/assets/*`

## Data Model
- `quizzes(id, title)`
- `questions(id, quiz_id, body, active, position)` ordered by position
- `options(id, question_id, body, is_correct, position)` ordered by position
- Move up/down swaps `position` with neighbor; gaps tolerated

## Key Behaviors
- Quiz form: Title required (HTML + server), Save redirects to quiz page
- Question form: 4 empty rows for new; JS `Add option` appends `Option N` + `Option N is correct` with correct `for`/`id`/`name` (`option_text_N`, `option_correct_N`); empty trimmed rows skipped; needs >=2 and >=1 correct; on fail re-render with raw typed rows + errors, no DB write
- Quiz page: `ul.question-list > li` per question, active numbered 1..N, inactive `—` + dimmed; Move buttons always enabled (no-op at ends); Active checkbox `onchange=submit` with hidden `_form` to detect unchecked; Edit link; Delete with `confirm()`
- Preview: only active in order; `GET /preview` -> `?q=0&score=0`; options as `POST /preview/answer` buttons; PRG to `?q&score&picked`; Correct!/Wrong! + `is-correct` reveal; Next/See score; `Score: X/N`; Start over single link per page to avoid Capybara ambiguity
- Lists: `ul.quiz-list > li` and `ul.question-list > li` with buttons inside li for QA scoping

## Offline
- `cargo vendor` + `.cargo/config.toml` source replacement ensures `cargo build --release --offline` works without registry cache
- `bin/serve` does `mkdir -p storage`, offline release build, exec; binds 0.0.0.0:$PORT, plain HTTP, any Host

## Design
- Reuses `docs/mockups/quizzy.css` + font as `assets/*`; admin layout matches mockups (header, page-head, cards, pill buttons); preview uses `.play` phone styles + `.preview-banner`

# Quizzy Moderator Release - Design Notes

## Architecture
- Rust + Axum 0.8 + Tokio + rusqlite (system SQLite, no bundled build for speed)
- Single binary `quizzy`, single file `src/main.rs` (~1300 lines)
- Per-request SQLite connections to `storage/quizzy.sqlite` with WAL + foreign_keys
- Stateless preview via URL query params (`q`, `score`, `picked`), no session storage
- Basic auth middleware for all `/moderate*` (401 + WWW-Authenticate on fail)
- Static assets embedded via `include_str!/include_bytes!` served at `/assets/*`

## Data Model
- `quizzes(id, title)`
- `questions(id, quiz_id, body, active, position)` ordered by position
- `options(id, question_id, body, is_correct, position)` ordered by position
- Move up/down swaps `position` with neighbor; gaps tolerated

## Key Behaviors
- Quiz form: Title required (HTML + server), Save redirects to quiz page
- Question form: 4 empty rows for new; JS `Add option` appends `Option N` + `Option N is correct` with correct `for`/`id`/`name` (`option_text_N`, `option_correct_N`); empty trimmed rows skipped; needs >=2 and >=1 correct; on fail re-render with raw typed rows + errors, no DB write
- Quiz page: `ul.question-list > li` per question, active numbered 1..N, inactive `—` + dimmed; Move buttons always enabled (no-op at ends); Active checkbox `onchange=submit` with hidden `_form` to detect unchecked; Edit link; Delete with `confirm()`
- Preview: only active in order; `GET /preview` -> `?q=0&score=0`; options as `POST /preview/answer` buttons; PRG to `?q&score&picked`; Correct!/Wrong! + `is-correct` reveal; Next/See score; `Score: X/N`; Start over single link per page to avoid Capybara ambiguity
- Lists: `ul.quiz-list > li` and `ul.question-list > li` with buttons inside li for QA scoping

## Offline
- `cargo vendor` + `.cargo/config.toml` source replacement ensures `cargo build --release --offline` works without registry cache
- `bin/serve` does `mkdir -p storage`, offline release build, exec; binds 0.0.0.0:$PORT, plain HTTP, any Host

## Design
- Reuses `docs/mockups/quizzy.css` + font as `assets/*`; admin layout matches mockups (header, page-head, cards, pill buttons); preview uses `.play` phone styles + `.preview-banner`
